Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1759.

## Problem

PR #1759 corrects `disinto-factory/operations.md`, which told operators to `nomad job restart agents`. That job is not the live runtime: `nomad/jobs/agents.hcl` is the pre-split all-roles job, stopped on the live box (`nomad/jobs/agents-dev-qwen.hcl` says `agents.hcl` is stopped), and `.woodpecker/ci.yml` skips basename `agents` so a deploy does not register a second polling loop (#1522).

The same command is still the documented operator action in:

- `docs/agents-llama.md` (per-env TOML reload): `nomad job restart agents`
- `docs/nomad-migration.md` (migrating existing boxes): `nomad job restart agents`
- `docs/updating-factory.md` Step 2 example: `nomad job run /opt/disinto/nomad/jobs/agents.hcl`, and Step 3 loops `nomad/jobs/agents*.hcl`, which includes `agents.hcl`, then `nomad job restart` on that basename

An operator who follows those steps can restart a stopped all-roles job or register a second polling loop beside the per-role jobs (`agents-dev-qwen`, `agents-review-qwen`, `agents-gardener-qwen`, `agents-supervisor-opus`, and the grok jobs).

## Expected

Point those commands at the live per-role jobs, and do not `nomad job run` / `nomad job restart` the basename `agents` job.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*



## Affected files
- docs/agents-llama.md
- docs/nomad-migration.md
- docs/updating-factory.md

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] docs/agents-llama.md per-env TOML reload uses the live per-role jobs (no `nomad job restart agents`)
- [ ] docs/nomad-migration.md uses the live per-role jobs (no `nomad job restart agents`)
- [ ] docs/updating-factory.md Step 2 no longer runs `nomad job run .../agents.hcl`
- [ ] docs/updating-factory.md Step 3 no longer restarts the stopped all-roles `agents.hcl` basename
- [ ] Grep for the stopped `agents` basename as an instructed operator action returns nothing

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1773.

## Problem

`lib/formula-session.sh` still documents a contract #1646 removed. Lines 410–412 say `dev-agent.sh` exports `TAPE_RUN_ATTEMPTS` as `ATTEMPT+1` from its branch-count block, and that recovery mode or a failed `ls-remote` leaves `ATTEMPT` empty so the export is 1. Lines 493–494 repeat that provenance. The resolver (positive integer, else 1) is still right; the provenance is not.

The live export is `TAPE_RUN_ATTEMPTS=$((DEV_FAILED_ATTEMPTS + 1))` (`dev/dev-agent.sh` around line 978), counted from the proposal's failed tape outcomes, not the branch count. `dev/AGENTS.md` already says the old `TAPE_RUN_ATTEMPTS="${ATTEMPT:0:0}"` block is removed. Restoring the branch-count export to match the `formula-session.sh` comments would put the retry cap back on `ATTEMPT`, which stays 0 when a run pushes nothing — the failure #1646 fixed.

The same stale sentence is still in `tests/acceptance/issue-1478.sh` (the "After" header and the AC 3 parenthetical). #1753 scoped that file to deleting the dead grep and keeping AC 1–3 unchanged, so the header contradiction was left in place. The executable checks are correct; the comments are not.

## Fix

Update those comments to the tape-driven count (`DEV_FAILED_ATTEMPTS + 1`). Do not restore the branch-count export.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*


## Affected files
- lib/formula-session.sh
- tests/acceptance/issue-1478.sh

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] lib/formula-session.sh comments (lines 410-412, 493-494) describe TAPE_RUN_ATTEMPTS provenance as the tape-driven count (DEV_FAILED_ATTEMPTS + 1), not the removed branch-count (ATTEMPT)
- [ ] The branch-count export is NOT restored in dev/dev-agent.sh
- [ ] tests/acceptance/issue-1478.sh header and AC-3 parenthetical reference the tape-driven count
- [ ] Executable checks in tests/acceptance/issue-1478.sh remain unchanged (AC 1-3 intact)

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1775.

## Problem

#1758 removes the Claude binary and credential mounts from `docker/edge/dispatcher.sh` on the claim that runners and sidecars no longer need them because `AGENT_HARNESS` defaults to dsh (#1683). That default only covers `lib/agent-sdk.sh` `agent_run`. These callers do not use it:

- `docker/reproduce/entrypoint-reproduce.sh` fatals if `claude` is not on `PATH` (expects a host mount of `/usr/local/bin/claude`) and then runs `claude -p`. `docker/reproduce/Dockerfile` does not install the CLI. `_dispatch_sidecar_docker` is the only implemented sidecar backend (`_dispatch_sidecar_nomad` returns 1) and is what `dispatch_reproduce`, `dispatch_triage`, and `dispatch_verify` launch (`disinto-reproduce:latest`).
- `docker/runner/entrypoint-runner.sh` `exec`s `claude -p` for every `formulas/<name>.toml` vault action. It does not consult `AGENT_HARNESS`. On the edge job, auth is the `claude-shared` OAuth mount (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (explicitly unset in `nomad/jobs/edge.hcl`).

Until those entrypoints move to the dsh harness (or stop calling Claude), the dispatcher mounts are load-bearing. Dropping them makes sidecar launches exit 1 and makes `.toml` vault formulas fail closed.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*


## Affected files
- docker/edge/dispatcher.sh
- docker/reproduce/entrypoint-reproduce.sh
- docker/reproduce/Dockerfile
- docker/runner/entrypoint-runner.sh
- nomad/jobs/edge.hcl

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sidecar launches (dispatch_reproduce, dispatch_triage, dispatch_verify) no longer exit 1 after the #1758 mount removal
- [ ] Either the reproduce/runner entrypoints move to the dsh harness or the required claude mounts are restored so sidecars and vault formulas succeed
- [ ] docker/reproduce/entrypoint-reproduce.sh does not fatal on a missing `claude` binary when the dsh harness is the default
- [ ] docker/runner/entrypoint-runner.sh dispatches formulas/*.toml vault actions via the dsh harness (AGENT_HARNESS) instead of execing `claude -p`
- [ ] No .toml vault formula fails closed on the edge job
